FN-O7GEWJ-1
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 5
Committee: State Governmental Affairs Sponsor: Senator Linda Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/17/2023
Senate Bill 5 as introduced provides that in the event the Board of Pardons and Paroles
establishes and maintains more than one residential transition centers for parolees and
probationers ordered to serve a period of confinement, at least one of the centers must be used as
a women's facility. This bill will not otherwise affect state or local funding.

FN-O7GEWJ-2
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 5
Committee: State Governmental Affairs Sponsor: Senator Linda Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 03/22/2023
Senate Bill 5 as reported by the Committee on State Governmental Affairs provides that in the
event the Board of Pardons and Paroles establishes and maintains more than one residential
transition centers for parolees and probationers ordered to serve a period of confinement, at least
one of the centers must be used as a women's facility. This bill will not otherwise affect state or
local funding.

FN-O7GEWJ-3
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 5
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Linda Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/20/2023
Senate Bill 5 as passed the Senate would require the Board of Pardons and Paroles to designate
one residential transition center as a women's facility, if the Board establishes any residential
transition centers as provided by current law. This bill would increase the obligations of the
Board, by an undetermined amount, to establish and maintain this women's facility, as the Board
currently operates a men's residential transition center.

FN-O7GEWJ-4
FISCAL NOTE
Senate Bill 5
Committee: Ways and Means General Fund Sponsor: Senator Linda Coleman-Madison
Analyst: Peter Grogan Date: 04/26/2023
Senate Bill 5 as reported by the Committee on Ways and Means General Fund would (1)
increase the minimum number of residential transition centers that the Board of Pardons and
Paroles may establish and maintain from one or more, under current law, to two or more; and
(2) require the board to designate one residential transition center as a women's facility. This bill
would increase the obligations of the board by an undetermined amount to establish and
maintain this women's facility, as the board currently operates a men's residential transition
center.
